ext.description: AI coding agent for VS Code with Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, Grok, and OpenAI-compatible APIs. Plan tasks, use workspace tools, load skills on demand, orchestrate several providers with your own API keys, run sub-agents, workflows and swarms, connect MCP servers, plugins and your Chrome, and keep a long-term memory.
cmd.openInTab: Open AI assistant in a new tab
cmd.fix: Find and fix bugs in selected code
cfg.defaultModel: Provider and model for new conversations, as `provider:model`, e.g. `anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5`. Empty = use the last selection.
cfg.language: UI language and the assistant's default reply language.
cfg.fontFamily: Chat font. **Be Vietnam Pro** is designed for Vietnamese, so tone marks are clearest.
cfg.lineHeight: Line height. Vietnamese stacks diacritics, so keep it at 1.6 or above.
cfg.showThinking: Show the "Thinking" block when the provider returns reasoning content.
cfg.permissionMode: Default permission mode for new conversations.
cfg.allowBypass: Allow the **bypass all confirmations** mode. The assistant will edit files and run commands without asking — enable only if you understand the risk.
cfg.permissions.allow: **Allow without asking** rules, written as `tool(spec)`: `run_command(npm test:*)` (command prefix), `run_command(git diff*)`, `edit_file(src/**)`, `fetch_url(domain:github.com)`, `mcp__server__tool`. Compound commands must match in EVERY part; requests outside the workspace / secret files still ask. Rules in the project's `.vscode/settings.json` only apply after you confirm them (`/permissions`).
cfg.permissions.ask: **Always ask** rules (even in accept-edits mode), same syntax as `permissions.allow`. Projects may add these.
cfg.permissions.deny: **Always block** rules (even in bypass mode), same syntax as `permissions.allow`, e.g. `read_file(.env*)`, `run_command(git push*)`. Projects may add these.
cfg.permissions.trustedWorkspaceAllow: Content hashes of workspace allow-rule lists you have confirmed (written by `/permissions trust`). Remove an entry to be asked again.
cfg.thinkingLevel: Default reasoning level. Each provider maps it to its own parameters; non-reasoning models ignore it.
cfg.checkpointsEnabled: Snapshot each file before the assistant first edits it in a turn, so **Rewind to this point**, `/rewind` and the “N files changed” bar can restore it. Stored in the extension data folder (last 30 turns per conversation, 14 days; files over 2 MB or binary are skipped). Files changed by shell commands are not tracked.
cfg.maxTurns: Maximum loop iterations for one request (each = one model call + tool execution). Default 200 — effectively no cap, like Claude Code; on reaching the limit the assistant still gets one wrap-up turn instead of stopping mid-task. Lower it only to cap cost.
cfg.budgetGuard: With ≤ 3 turns left, block EXPLORATORY tools (reading files, searching, fetching pages) so the assistant wraps up instead of exploring further; writing/editing files and running checks stay allowed. If nothing was written or run yet, one final read is still allowed for a meaningful wrap-up. Turn off to let the assistant decide until the last turn.
cfg.shellCheck: Check commands before `run_command` runs them, against the machine's real shell. `rewrite` (default): simple `a && b` / `a || b` on Windows PowerShell 5.1 is rewritten to `a; if ($?) { b }`, complex forms are blocked with guidance, and other bash habits (`grep`, `export`, `rm -rf`, `/dev/null`…) are only hinted in the result. `hint`: never change the command, only hint. `off`: disabled.
cfg.loopBreaker: Result-based loop breaker: the same tool returning the same result 3 times in a row (even with slightly different arguments) gets a change-strategy note; a 4th near-identical call is blocked. Turn off if your tools intentionally return identical results.
cfg.maxOutputTokens: Maximum tokens the model may generate in one call (including reasoning tokens).
cfg.adaptiveOutputTokens: Pick the output limit per turn by task type: 8,000 tokens for ordinary answers / comparisons / code edits; the full limit (`maxOutputTokens`, clamped to the model's real limit) when writing reports, long documents, full versions, or continuing a cut-off reply. Off = always use the full limit.
cfg.modelStallSeconds: Anti-hang watchdog: how long the model may stay silent before that single call is cancelled and retried once (time spent in the Locaith gateway queue does not count). `auto` (default) = by context size (20 s under 32k · 45 s up to 200k · 70 s up to 600k · 90 s above) times a reasoning factor (medium ×1.5 · high ×2.5 · max ×4). `0` = off. Or a fixed number of seconds (5–600).
cfg.modelCallMaxSeconds: Hard cap on the active time of ONE model call (seconds, 30–3600; default 600). When exceeded the call is cancelled, what was written is kept and a "Continue" button is shown.
cfg.parallelToolCalls: Let the model issue several tool calls at once (e.g. parallel web searches).
cfg.verify: Independent check (blind reviewer): when the assistant is about to report completion, a verifier agent with a CLEAN context (it sees only the original request, changed files, commands run and the final answer — never the reasoning) reads and runs tests/typecheck itself, then rules. On failure the assistant must address every item (up to 2 rounds); anything still outstanding is reported honestly. /verify runs it manually.
cfg.verify.auto: Runs when the turn changed files, or ran 3+ commands over 4+ loop turns, with reasoning level medium or higher. Pure Q&A never triggers it.
cfg.verify.always: Runs after every turn (except Stop / loop budget exhausted / refusal).
cfg.verifyModel: Model for the verifier agent as `provider:model` (e.g. `anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5`). Empty = same model as the assistant. Read from user settings only.
cfg.compactAtPercent: Auto-compact once the context is this percentage of the model's window (50-95, default 80). Compacting too early makes the assistant forget what it was doing; use 90 for models with a large window.
cfg.compactAtTokens: Absolute cap (tokens) for the compaction threshold: effective threshold = min(compactAtPercent × window, cap). 0 = automatic: a 300,000-token cap applies ONLY to models with a window above 400k and only when you have NOT set compactAtPercent yourself (windows ≤ 400k keep the old behaviour). Huge contexts make every turn several times slower.
cfg.clearToolResultsAtPercent: Start clearing old tool results (read_file, run_command…) once the context exceeds this percentage of the window (default 40; 0 = off). Each cleared result becomes one line with the tool name, path/command, ok or error (with exit code) and a hint to call it again — the assistant can re-read whenever needed. The 8 most recent results and the step awaiting a reply are always kept. Clearing runs in batches down to ~30%.
cfg.keepRecentMessages: Number of most recent messages kept verbatim when the whole conversation is summarized (4-200, default 20). The cut point moves back to a turn boundary, so a tool call is never separated from its result.
cfg.autoCompact: Automatically compact older messages when the context is nearly full.
cfg.instructionFiles: Project instruction files loaded into the system prompt if present in the workspace root (first one found wins).
cfg.summarizerEnabled: Run a small background model that turns the thinking/code-writing stream into short status lines. Costs a few extra tokens.
cfg.summarizerModel: `auto` = pick a cheap, fast model from the same provider. Or set `provider:model`, e.g. `gemini:gemini-3.5-flash-lite`.
cfg.editDiagnostics: After the assistant edits/writes a file, wait about a second for the language server, then tell the assistant about **new** errors in that file (pre-existing ones are not repeated) so it fixes them before reporting done.
cfg.editDiagnostics.off: Off: never read diagnostics after edits.
cfg.contextEditor: Automatically attach the active file name and current selection as context to every message. Click the “Viewing” chip in the composer to toggle it quickly.
cfg.searchBackend: Backend for the `web_search` tool. Brave/Tavily/Serper API keys are stored in SecretStorage via **Set API key…**.
cfg.searxngUrl: Your SearXNG server URL (when `searxng` is selected), e.g. `https://searx.example.com`.
cfg.shell: Shell used by the `run_command` tool. `auto` = PowerShell on Windows, bash/zsh on macOS/Linux.
cfg.commandTimeout: Maximum seconds for each terminal command before it is stopped.
cfg.allowPrivate: Let `fetch_url` reach private network addresses (localhost, 192.168.x.x…). Off by default to prevent being tricked into reading internal data.
cfg.skillPaths: Extra skill folders (each skill is a folder containing `SKILL.md`). `.locaith/skills` and `.claude/skills` in the workspace are always scanned.
cfg.baseUrls: Override base URLs of built-in providers, e.g. `{ "openai": "https://my-proxy.example.com/v1" }`. Your API key is sent to these addresses, so this is read from **user** settings only (never from a workspace's `.vscode/settings.json`) and must be https (http only for localhost / private network).
cfg.artifactsAutoOpen: When to open the artifact preview automatically. By default only SVG/Markdown open by themselves; model-written HTML with scripts opens only when you click "Open" on the artifact card. Read from user settings only.
cfg.customProviders: Add custom APIs (OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, Groq, Together, vLLM…). `kind` defaults to `openai-chat`.
cfg.eagerInput: For Claude: ask the API to stream tool arguments (long source code) incrementally. Turn off behind a proxy that does not support it.
cfg.debug: Log request/response details (keys masked) to the output channel.
cfg.orchestrationMode: Multi-AI orchestration, based only on the API keys you have entered. `off` (default) uses just the selected model; `failover` switches provider when rate-limited/overloaded; `auto` also lets sub-agents and workflows pick models by tier and spread load across providers. Pick the "Locaith Auto" model to delegate model choice entirely. Read from user settings only.
cfg.mcpServers: MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that give the assistant external tools. Each entry is `{ "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "package"], "env": {…} }` or `{ "url": "https://…" }`. Servers declared here start automatically; servers from a workspace `.mcp.json` only run after you enable them in the Market. Read from user settings only.
cfg.pluginPaths: Folders containing plugins (each subfolder is a plugin bundling skills, agents, commands, MCP). `~/.locaith/plugins` and the workspace `.locaith/plugins` are always scanned. Newly found plugins stay disabled until you enable them.
cfg.agentsMaxConcurrent: Maximum number of sub-agents running at once in one conversation (1–16). Each provider also has its own cap to avoid rate limits.
cfg.commandsReadClaudeDir: Also read custom slash commands from `.claude/commands` (Claude Code compatible). A project's `.claude` folder is only read when the workspace is trusted; `.locaith/commands` is always read.
cfg.agentOutputStyle: Default reply style for new conversations: `default`, `explanatory` (adds short “why” insights), `learning` (leaves small pieces for you to write), `concise`, or the name of a file in `.locaith/output-styles`. Change per conversation with `/output-style`. A style only changes tone; it never relaxes safety rules.
cmd.openMarket: Open the Market (skills, plugins, MCP, agents)
cmd.remotePair: Remote: pair a new device (code + link)
cmd.remoteManage: Remote: paired devices / stop remote control
cfg.chromeBridge: Bridge to the Locaith AI extension on Chrome/Edge — **ON BY DEFAULT**: VS Code opens a local port (127.0.0.1, extension origins only) so Chrome can ask to connect WITHOUT A CODE; every pairing shows an “Allow / Deny” card in the chat and needs your Allow. Turn off to open no port at all (then you can only pair with a code in Market → Chrome).
cfg.remoteEnabled: Remote control (the “VS Code remote” tab on locaith.ai views and controls this chat) — **ON BY DEFAULT** once you are signed in to your Locaith account: the machine joins the end-to-end encrypted relay and shows up in “Your machines” (the machine name and project folder name are stored in your account). A browser signed in to THIS Locaith account opens the machine right away, no pairing needed (see `locaithAgent.remote.trustAccount`); people without your account cannot. A browser that gets in can do anything the assistant can do on this machine (read/edit files, run commands according to the permission mode in use). Turn it off to disconnect from the relay completely. Type **/remote** in the chat to open the Remote page directly.
cfg.remoteWebUrl: Address of the Remote page that the pairing command opens (default https://locaith.ai). When developing the site on this machine set `http://localhost:3000` — that origin is automatically allowed to call in.
cfg.remoteOrigins: Origins of web pages allowed to call the Remote server (exact match, e.g. `https://locaith.ai`). Any other origin is rejected on every path.
cfg.remotePublicUrl: Public address if you expose the Remote server yourself through a tunnel (e.g. `https://vscode.example.com`). Empty = usable on this machine only. This host name is added to the accepted Host headers and used in pairing links.
cfg.remoteIdleDays: A device not used for this many days is revoked and must be paired again.
cfg.remoteAllowBypass: Let a remote device switch the assistant to **bypass all confirmations** mode by itself. Off by default: that mode can only be set in VS Code.
cfg.remoteTrustAccount: Trust your account — **ON BY DEFAULT**: a browser signed in to YOUR Locaith account opens this VS Code right from locaith.ai (phone, another computer) with NO pairing code/link and no “Allow” prompt. In exchange, anyone who can sign in to your Locaith account can control this machine — protect the account with a strong password/two-factor sign-in. Off = back to pairing each device with a link/QR + “Allow” (devices already paired keep working). To cut every browser that is currently in without turning it off: **Remote: paired devices / stop remote control** → “Change the account key”. Read from user settings only.
cmd.accountEnterCode: Account: paste sign-in code (when the browser cannot return to VS Code)
cfg.remoteCloud: Allow remote control **over the Internet** (locaith.ai relay, end-to-end encrypted) when Remote is on and you are signed in to Locaith. Off = local path only. Devices paired this way work from a phone/another computer.
cfg.remoteLocal: Allow remote control **on this machine only** (local 127.0.0.1 server, no network) when Remote is on. OFF by default: no port is opened on your machine; turn it on when you want to use the Remote page right on this machine.
